rounds.text: Uniparts India Ltd is operating with exceptional profitability and return metrics that comfortably outpace sector benchmarks, demonstrated by an ROA of 14.38% against 5.98%, an ROE of 18.19% against 11.38%, and an ROCE of 21.06% against 12.27% [E8, E9, E10]. This fundamental strength translates into powerful recent operational acceleration, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 88%, a quarterly operating margin reaching 24% in June 2026, and a robust new business order book exceeding INR 225 crores [E19, E26, E83]. Furthermore, the business is backed by pristine cash generation, shown by a cash conversion ratio of 1.10x with free cash flow of INR 148 crores and a conservatively financed balance sheet featuring a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.18x [E29, E31, E33]. Management visibility supports continued outperformance, with expected FY27 revenue growth exceeding FY26 levels by a couple of percentage points alongside new catalysts like the upcoming Mexico warehouse deliveries and steady infrastructure demand in the U.S. and Europe [E71, E74, E78]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of 5.32% over the past five years and a negative 3-year compounded sales growth of -5% [E15, E56].

Uniparts India Ltd trades at a price-to-book ratio of 4.42x, which sits above the sector benchmark of 2.8x [E7], while its EV/EBITDA of 13.69x also exceeds the sector benchmark of 12.62x [E11]. Beneath the recent TTM momentum, the company has delivered a poor compounded sales growth of 5.32% over the past five years [E56], alongside negative 3-year compounded sales growth of -5% [E15] and negative 3-year compounded profit growth of -8% [E18]. Furthermore, domestic institutional holdings have dropped significantly from 11.04% in September 2023 to 4.94% as of June 2026 [E39], indicating institutional capital withdrawal. The business is also exposed to cyclical demand volatility, with tariff-driven price volatility and macroeconomic uncertainty leading to demand deferrals and customer purchasing moderation in the aftermarket [E90], compounded by ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia exerting pressure on input costs and supply chains [E89]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong ROE of 18.3% [E13] and rules-based screening scores of 87 out of 100 [E57].

Conceded: price-to-book of 4.42x sits above the sector benchmark of 2.8x [E7], and EV/EBITDA of 13.69x exceeds the sector benchmark of 12.62x [E11]. However, that premium valuation is entirely justified by superior returns on capital, as ROA reaches 14.38% against a sector benchmark of 5.98% [E8] and ROCE hits 21.06% against a sector benchmark of 12.27% [E10]. While 3-year sales and profit growth show past cyclical softness at -5% and -8% [E15, E18], trailing twelve-month figures demonstrate a powerful turnaround with 27% sales growth and 88% profit growth [E16, E19]. The decline in domestic institutional holding [E39] is offset by positive overall institutional money flow [E40], while strong fundamentals are evidenced by a robust net cash position of approximately INR 190 crores [E86] and operating cash flow backing profits fully at 1.10x conversion [E29]. Finally, external supply chain and aftermarket pressures [E89, E90] are successfully mitigated by strong order visibility from U.S. and European infrastructure spending [E74] alongside a robust trailing twelve-month new business order book of over INR 225 crores [E83].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month figures show 27% sales growth and 88% profit growth [E16, E19], and operating cash flow backs profit fully at 1.10x conversion [E29]. However, pointing to superior ROCE of 21.06% [E10] ignores the fact that the price-to-book of 4.42x and EV/EBITDA of 13.69x already price in these metrics at a heavy premium to their respective sector benchmarks of 2.8x and 12.62x [E7, E11]. The bullish reliance on a net cash position of roughly INR 190 crores [E86] overlooks the reality that total borrowings climbed to Rs 155 Cr from Rs 120 Cr a year earlier [E35]. Furthermore, citing positive institutional money flow [E40] glosses over the sharp withdrawal by domestic institutions, whose holding plunged from 11.04% in September 2023 to 4.94% by June 2026 [E39]. While a new business order book of over INR 225 crores is highlighted [E83], management explicitly notes that ongoing West Asia tensions continue to pressure supply chains and input costs [E89], alongside tariff-driven price volatility and macroeconomic uncertainty that are deferring customer purchasing decisions in the aftermarket [E90, E91]. Finally, the claim of a powerful turnaround is undermined by the 3-year compounded sales contraction of -5% and profit contraction of -8% [E15, E18], coupled with an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend [E27].

Conceded: domestic institutional holdings dropped from 11.04% in September 2023 to 4.94% in June 2026 [E39], and total borrowings rose to Rs 155 Cr from Rs 120 Cr [E35]. However, total borrowings are heavily outweighed by a robust net cash position of approximately INR 190 crores [E86] and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E33]. While the bear cites valuation premiums over sector benchmarks [E7, E11], Uniparts' superior return metrics—such as an ROE of 18.19% versus the sector's 11.38% and ROCE of 21.06% against 12.27% [E9, E10]—fully justify a higher multiple. The bear's focus on past multi-year contractions [E15, E18] ignores the explosive current inflection, evidenced by TTM sales growth leaping 27% and profit surging 88% [E16, E19]. Finally, management's commentary on geopolitical pressures [E89, E90] is balanced by strong operational visibility, including a trailing twelve-month new business order book over INR 225 crores [E83] and expectations that full-year FY27 revenue growth will exceed FY26 [E71].

Conceded: the company holds a net cash position of approximately INR 190 crores and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E33, E86]. However, the bull's dismissal of rising debt ignores that borrowings climbed to Rs 155 Cr from Rs 120 Cr a year earlier [E35]. Furthermore, pointing to superior return metrics [E9, E10] glosses over the sector comparisons showing Uniparts trading at a stretched Price-to-Book ratio of 4.42x against a sector benchmark of 2.8x, alongside an EV/EBITDA of 13.69x exceeding the sector's 12.62x [E7, E11]. The bull celebrates recent TTM surges of 27% in sales and 88% in profit [E16, E19], but this hides a poor structural history of a 5.32% compounded sales growth over five years [E56], coupled with multi-year contractions of -5% in 3-year sales and -8% in 3-year profits [E15, E18]. Conceded: the TTM order book stands at over INR 225 crores [E83] and FY27 revenue is expected to grow [E71], yet management explicitly warns that West Asian geopolitical tensions, tariff-driven price volatility, and economic uncertainty continue to pressure input costs and defer big-ticket consumer purchases in the aftermarket [E89, E90, E91]. Finally, the massive institutional exodus—with domestic institutions slashing their holdings from 11.04% to 4.94%—demonstrates that sophisticated investors are actively retreating despite the short-term earnings inflection [E39].

evidence.quote: keeping that in mind and the visibility that we have, our FY27 growth will be a couple of percentage points bigger than the growth that we had in FY26 on a year-on-year basis.

evidence.fact: Q2 FY27 operational performance is expected to remain robust and in line with Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: Q2 looks very robust, and I think Q2 should be in line with Q1.

evidence.fact: Mexico warehouse operations are projected to generate mid-single-digit million-dollar revenue in FY27.
evidence.quote: For FY27, we believe that this revenue should be in mid-single-digit million dollar level.

evidence.fact: Demand in construction equipment is being sustained by infrastructure spending in the U.S. and government investments in Europe.
evidence.quote: Infrastructure-led spending, particularly under the technology investments in the U.S. and the government-led investments in Europe, is sustaining healthy customer schedules and order visibility.

evidence.fact: Leading OEMs view calendar year 2026 as the cyclical bottom for large agricultural equipment, expecting recovery in calendar year 2027.
evidence.quote: Leading OEMs have indicated that current year 2026 represents the cyclical bottom with a more meaningful recovery expected through calendar year 2027.

evidence.fact: Small agricultural equipment in India is performing well, supported by government subsidy programs and increasing adoption in mid-to-higher horsepower categories.
evidence.quote: In the small agriculture equipment, India continues to perform well, supported by government subsidy programs and rising adoption across the mid-to-higher horsepower categories.

evidence.fact: Restoration of the finishing shop at the Ludhiana facility is progressing on schedule without causing customer supply disruption.
evidence.quote: On that note, the restoration of the finishing shop at our Ludhiana facility is progressing well and on schedule.

evidence.fact: First customer deliveries from the Mexico warehouse operations are expected to begin in Q3 of this fiscal year.
evidence.quote: Equally, our Mexico operations are on track with first customer deliveries from the warehouse expected in Q3 of this year.

evidence.fact: Capital expenditure during Q1 FY27 was INR 12 crores, focusing on capacity enhancement, productivity, and customer-led initiatives.
evidence.quote: Capital expenditure during the quarter was INR12 crores, in line with ongoing investment plans focused on capacity enhancement, productivity improvement and customer-led growth initiatives.

evidence.fact: EBITDA for Q1 FY27 reached INR 90 crores, marking a 55% year-on-year growth and 10% sequential growth.
evidence.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR90 crores, registering strong 55% growth year-on-year and 10% growth sequentially, reflecting healthy operating leverage and disciplined cost management across the business.

evidence.fact: Material cost in Q1 FY27 was 33.3%, primarily reflecting a shift in product mix.
evidence.quote: So Viraj, if you look at it, our cost of materials this time is about 33.3%, And I think it's coming at 33.3% largely because there's been a product mix change.

evidence.fact: Management maintains that material costs normally range between 34% and 37% over the business cycle.
evidence.quote: I think what we've always maintained is that our material cost should be in the range of 34% to 37%, and that's typical of our business.

evidence.quote: On the business development front, our trailing 12-month new business order book remains robust at over INR225 crores with a healthy pipeline.

evidence.quote: Ashutosh, you are right that in Q1 FY27, the business has really seen a good growth in the construction business, which is today 45% of our total revenue.

evidence.quote: Our net cash position at the end of quarter 1 stands at INR190 crores, reflecting the continued strength of our cash generation.

evidence.quote: We generated INR44 crores of operating cash during the quarter, and our 12-month trailing EPS stands at INR39.97, reflecting sustained improvement in earnings over the past year.

evidence.quote: I think today, we have about half a dozen opportunities that we are closely looking at.
